title: Contingent Capacity Sink & Leapfrog Plan — Feb 2026
summary: Working sheet describing a complementary strategy to our existing warm-pool approach: designate lightweight regional 'capacity sinks' to temporarily absorb redirected inference load and a 'leapfrog' provisioning pattern to bring nearby region capacity online rapidly. Includes inventory snapshots, scenario scoring, playbook steps for manual and automated execution, and high-level cost tradeoffs.
key_assumptions: Typical global steady-state GPU utilization: 68% (Jan 2026 observed)
P99 latency SLOs must be maintained for hosted-api customers unless explicit downgrade allowed
Inter-region provisioning time (cold to warm): 9-18 minutes without preemption-friendly config; 3-6 minutes with pre-warmed containers + KV cache sync
Network egress budgets can absorb up to 1.2x redirected traffic for short windows (validated in stress tests)
Preemptible instances allowed for non-SLA traffic and dedicated burst under cost-tier rules
regional_inventory: us-west1: 520 GPUs (A100-equivalent), 40 node slots reserved for experiments, current spare headroom ~8%
us-east4: 360 GPUs (A100-equivalent), configured as primary warm-pool, spare headroom ~12%
europe-west2: 300 GPUs, regional KV cache replication enabled, spare headroom ~10%
asia-southeast1: 220 GPUs, limited ephemeral quota, spare headroom ~6%
canada-central1: 120 GPUs, used as cold pool, spare headroom ~18% when unthrottled
target_headroom: Baseline: 10% headroom per region for normal ops. Contingent target: 25% absorbable capacity across the cluster for 30-minute windows during incidents.
scenarios_considered: Single region outage (compute facility) — traffic redistributed to 2 neighboring regions
Cascading throttles from a noisy tenant — per-tenant isolation + capacity sink soak
Provider-side preemption spike in a region — leapfrog to adjacent region + ephemeral preemptible burst
Network partition between control plane and region — route around with local sinks and degraded KV freshness
Coordinated promotional traffic surge (marketing event) — short-duration 2x load burst
playbook_steps: Detect: SRE alert + automated degradation score > 0.6 triggers 'contingent mode'
Sink engage (automated): Mark target region as sink — set traffic weighting to 0.75 for non-SLA flows; enable prefix caching to reduce per-token compute
Leapfrog provision (automated): Trigger nearest-region autoscale policy with pre-warmed container image and KV snapshot restore; provisioning window target 3-6m
Manual override: On-call infra to run 'force-leapfrog' script (infra/tools/force_leapfrog.sh) to bypass rate-limiters for enterprise tenants
Stabilize: Run a 15m soak with continuous monitoring of error-rates, tail latency, and egress budgets
Demote sink: Gradually reduce sink weighting only after 30m of stable metrics and when origin region reports healthy resource states
capacity_transfer_mechanisms: Two mechanisms: 1) Short-term traffic sink routing: change traffic weights at the load-router layer and enable KV-prefetch to reduce cold-cache cost. 2) Leapfrog provisioning: spin up warm instances in adjacent region with KV snapshot transfer. Leapfrog uses smaller instance profiles first (fractional-quantized models) and progressively migrates to full cards if sustained demand remains.
cost_estimates: Estimated incremental cost for a 30-minute single-region failover using leapfrog + sinks: $8.2k (preemptible-first), $22k (on-demand warm nodes). Monthly reserve to cover 3 such events with conservative margin: $66k.
risk_matrix_notes: Primary risks: longer-than-expected KV sync causing cold latency spikes; cross-region egress limits; mistaken sink weight causing SLA violation for enterprise routes. Mitigations: staged weighting, tenant-level exemptions, egress rate limiter alarms, and automated rollback policy in the router.
simulation_results_ref: Simulation workbook: drives/analysis/infra/contingent-simulations-2026.xlsx (sheet: 'leapfrog_runs') — runs include stochastic tenant-noise and preemption models.
